    Screen corpus using regex matching

    Source: R/question-screen.R
    sm_screen_regex.Rd

    A deterministic screening method that uses regular expression matching on work titles and abstracts. Works matching any include_terms (case-insensitive) and none of the exclude_terms are classified as "include"; works matching an exclude term are "exclude"; works matching no include term are "exclude".

    Usage

    sm_screen_regex(
  corpus,
  include_terms,
  exclude_terms = NULL,
  unicode = TRUE,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object.

    include_terms

    Character vector of regex patterns. A work must match at least one to be included.

    exclude_terms

    Character vector of regex patterns. A work matching any is excluded. Default NULL (no exclusions).

    unicode

    Logical (default TRUE). Match the terms in Unicode mode, so \w, \b, \d, \s and POSIX classes know non-ASCII letters, digits and spaces, as in German or French titles. FALSE gives ASCII-only classes.

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    A modified sm_corpus with updated screening table.

    Details

    Terms are Perl-compatible regular expressions (PCRE), matched as written and case-insensitively against the title and abstract of each work. In Unicode mode (the default) each term is prefixed with the PCRE item (*UCP) unless its leading items already include it, so \b finds the edge of a word that starts with an umlaut and \w consumes one. A term can therefore also stop matching: one that used \W, \S, \D or \B to stand for a non-ASCII letter no longer matches it, and \b no longer finds an edge between an ASCII letter and a non-ASCII letter next to it, as inside a German compound word. Write [A-Za-z0-9_] instead of \w for an ASCII-only class.

    See also

    Other question: is_sm_question(), sm_corpus_for_question(), sm_question(), sm_screen_against_question(), sm_screen_summary()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus(n_works = 20, n_authors = 5)
screened <- sm_screen_regex(corpus,
                            include_terms = c("spatial", "transcriptom"),
                            exclude_terms = "\\bmouse\\b")
#> ✔ Regex screening: 7 included, 13 excluded.
sm_screen_summary(screened)
#> 
#> ── Stage: regex (n=20) 
#> exclude: 13 (65%)
#> include: 7 (35%)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   stage decision     n   pct
#>   <chr> <chr>    <int> <dbl>
#> 1 regex exclude     13    65
#> 2 regex include      7    35
